subject: priors hierarchical ordered IRT/Problem computing cutpoints

messages.author: ccc4693ce4e025f0
messages.subject: priors hierarchical ordered IRT/Problem computing cutpoints
parts:
Hi, 

I am working with a survey experiment that I am analyzing using a polytomous IRT. I have been struggling with some computational problems, and also could use some help in how to deal with priors.

My model is something like this:

beta_l ~ normal(x_l *theta, sigma) 

this models the trait of individual l as a function of covariates x_l and

y_lq ~ orderedlogit(treatment*beta_l + phi_q) 
 
which models the response y_lq of individual l to question q as a function of the difficulty of the question phi_q and whether it is exposed to the treatment or not. 

Here is my code so far:

data{
  int<lower=0> N; //n of observations
  int<lower = 1> D;// n of regressors
  int<lower=0> K;//n of answers
  int<lower=0> Q;//n of cases
  int<lower = 1> L;// n of individual
  int<lower=0, upper=Q> QQ[N];// vector of indicator cases
  int<lower=1, upper=L> ll[N];//vector of indicator individual
  int<lower=0, upper=4> y[N];//vector of outocome
  row_vector[D] x[N]; //matrix of regressors
  int<lower=0, upper=1> treat[N]; //vector treatment
}
parameters{
  vector[D] theta;//vector regressors of individual effects
  real<lower=0> sigma;//variance of individual effect
  positive_ordered[K-1] c[Q];//
  real phi[Q];//case effect
  real beta[L];//individual effect
}
model{
  c[Q] ~ normal(0,5);
  theta ~ normal(0,3);
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,5);
  for (n in 1:N){
    beta[ll[n]] ~ normal(x[n]*theta, sigma);
    y[n] ~ ordered_logistic(treat[n]*beta[ll[n]]+phi[QQ[n]],c[QQ[n]]);
  }
}



Now, I am getting this  error once and again.

Exception thrown at line 23: ordered_logistic: Cut points parameter is 0, but must be greater than 0     2
Exception thrown at line 23: ordered_logistic: Cut points parameter is 2.73902, but must be greater      1 
Exception thrown at line 23: ordered_logistic: Cut points parameter is 3.31566e+07, but must be grea 1 
....

Following the advice http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#exception-hamiltonian-proposal-rejected I've been trying to see what restriction I could add to facilitate the computational task for the cutpoints. Is there any prior I could use on cutpoints?  I have seen  this thread https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/pYkCZvrrkRg I have played with several specifications but have not got very far.

messages.author: 3d7541308bd2e290
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] priors hierarchical ordered IRT/Problem computing cutpoints
parts:
Howdy Luis

I suspect that you're getting this error because your 'y' is not in a valid range.

I think it needs to be greater than zero. In your data block, it's possible for it to be zero.

Have a look at the valid parameter ranges in the manual. Sometimes distributions are parameterized a little different in different bits of software so it's good to check.

Hope it works!

Ben
